blocks.text: The Guru warns that the betrayer Phatta will not escape the consequence of his act, while the journey pushes onward through inns and temporary halts under constant threat. (13–14)
The companions maintain the pose of a fasting pir, opening the fast ritually, speaking little, and moving carefully so that both devotion and disguise serve the same end. (15–16)

Some Singhs fear for their dharam in this setting, but the Guru reassures them that tyranny does not define true religion, and the party continues onward with food tied up for travel and fresh resolve. (17–21)
